newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Mark weakens on EMU jitters, Eurobourses dip.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Mark weakens on EMU jitters, Eurobourses dip.

text.p: The German mark weakened against the dollar and sterling on Monday as uncertainty over the European single currency unsettled traders and European bourses slipped, preoccupied by domestic issues.

London dipped slightly in cautious dealings ahead of Wednesday's budget, expected to contain bad news for investors. Frankfurt and Paris flitted in and out of profit before registering modest losses by midday.
The main action was in currency markets, where a new bout of nerves over European economic and monetary union (EMU) drove the dollar up by almost a pfennig to 1.7463 marks.
Sterling also rose to a five-year high against the German currency.

Traders hurried into safe haven currencies after a rift within German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's ruling alliance over EMU widened at the weekend with one of his partners raising the prospect of leaving the coalition.
"We are continuing to see this structural desire to shift out of core EMU currencies into alternatives," said Shean Shepley, international economist at CS First Boston.
The German dispute pits members of Kohl's Christian Democratic Union (CDU) against its Bavarian sister party, the Christian Social Union (CSU), and above all Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber.

Stoiber is calling for a delay in monetary union if the entry criteria are weakened. He has threatened to block German membership of EMU in the upper house of parliament unless the criteria are strictly met.
"Europe has big problems to get over and the way the politicians are going about it is not very constructive," Shepley added.
"Uncertainty over European monetary union is supporting the dollar and sterling," Nick Shamin, currency analyst at ANZ Investment, said.

The U.S. currency was further boosted by figures on Monday showing French unemployment rose 1.1 per cent in May. Traders said rising unemployment increased prospects of a delay to EMU or a soft euro from the outset.

With the German currency already vulnerable over EMU, sterling was given an added lift, reaching 2.9025 marks, when stronger-than-expected British data on consumer credit fuelled chances of an interest rate increase.

In equity markets, London opened higher but quickly turned negative with investors pulling in their horns ahead of the new Labour government's budget, amid talk that it could hit dividend tax breaks for pension funds.
In contrast to currency markets, the prospects of higher British interest rates had the effect of depressing stocks.
"There had been so much speculation about the budget and I can't see the major funds wanting to do anything for the next couple of days," said one dealer.
The market was also likely to be edgy this week ahead of a meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's monetary policy-makers, analysts said.
Few expect an immediate U.S. interest rate rise but the central bank is likely to be alert for any signs that the underlying strength of the economy could feed inflation in coming months.

Frankfurt initially made modest gains, underpinned by the stronger dollar, which helps exporters, and Friday's Wall Street gains. But the blue-chip DAX index ran out of steam by lunchtime and slipped into the minus column.
Paris shed its opening profits and was down 9.84 points at 2,881.20 on the CAC-40 index by midday..

Car-maker Renault fell 1.16 percent at 153.70 francs on profit-taking before recovering slightly. Brokers say the closure of the Vilvoorde plant in Belgium, confirmed over the weekend, was priced into the share.
In thin trading on bullion markets, gold was fixed at $334.05 an ounce, its lowest price for 4-1/2 years, under pressure from the strong dollar.
CURRENCIES AT 1130 GMT
The dollar was at 114.50 yen and 1.7463 marks, compared with 114.62 and 1.7365 in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1130 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 2.2 points at 4,638.1.
PARIS - The CAC-40 slipped 9.84 to 2,881.20.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 9.64 points at 3,785.77.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $334.05 an ounce against $337.15 at Friday's close. Silver was at $4.72, down two cents.
